questions.q: In what order do inspiring leaders communicate, according to Sinek?
a: Why, then how, then what
What, then how, then why
How, then what, then why
Why, then what, then how
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes leaders starting with purpose, then method, and revealing the product last.

questions.q: Why does starting with why work better than explaining what you do?
a: Emotions drive decisions more strongly than rational arguments
Customers always prefer the cheapest available option
Facts are impossible to remember over time
Companies cannot explain their products clearly
questions.why: Lesson 1 says emotions trump reason, so a strong why makes people own the decision.

questions.q: How does Apple illustrate the golden circle?
a: It explains its purpose first and only later names its products
It lists technical specifications before its mission
It advertises mainly through limited-time discounts
It lets retailers explain its products to customers
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Apple leads with its reason for existing and reveals computers and phones last.

questions.q: How many true fans does the summary say can sustain a business for a lifetime?
a: One thousand
One hundred
Ten thousand
One million
questions.why: Lesson 3 says a thousand true fans, who trust your why, are enough to keep a business going.
